test_title: SSC CPO 2024 Official Paper-I (Held On: 28 Jun, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Two statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

1) All games are tournaments.

2) Some tournaments are matches.

**Conclusions:**

I. All games are matches.

II. No game is a tournament.

options.text: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows.
Both Conclusions I and II follow.

solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/832576d3dc07153f8855b450020357bdb58c9a93f002a271d2f3962c85e9b91e.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All games are matches → Does not follow (As all games are tournaments and some tournaments are matches. So it is possible but not definite.)

II. No game is a tournament → Does not follow (As all games are tournaments. As whole games comes in tournament, therefore, game can not be tournament is false.)

∴ Here, Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follow.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows"
